LOOK: Kalikasan People’s Network for the Environment and PAMALAKAYA, along with other environmental advocates, fisherfolk, and indigenous peoples staged a protest in front of the Supreme Court in Manila today to commemorate World Environment Day.

The protest served as a response to two landmark decisions: nullifying the 25-year mining moratorium in Occidental Mindoro, and permitting commercial fishing vessels within the 15-kilometer municipal waters.

“These decisions effectively open up around 90% of our municipal waters to exploitation by large commercial fishing operations, jeopardizing the livelihoods of millions of small fisherfolks nationwide,” PAMALAKAYA Secretary General Salvador France added.

The groups warn that the Supreme Court’s ruling could set a dangerous precedent that threatens the ecosystem and continues to marginalize small-scale fisherfolk and indigenous peoples.

“By allowing large-scale mining and commercial fishing in areas previously protected, these decisions trample on the rights of local governments and communities to safeguard their environment and well-being," Jonila Castro of Kalikasan People's Network for the Environment said.

A noise barrage and a symbolic tearing of the Supreme Court’s decisions concluded the protest to symbolize the collective rejection of anti-people policies favoring destructive mining and fishing industries.

“Our lands are not for plunder, and our people will not bow to greed. The power to decide our future belongs to us, not to corporations, or corrupt officials,” Castro ended.

Report and photos from Rutchelle Ellema, JG / Altermidya
